piezas.titular: Cross-checking several AIs was a homemade trick; today Perplexity and Copilot do it for you
piezas.entradilla: In November 2025, the advice for trusting an answer was to ask several AIs and have another one look for the discrepancies. Today there are services that do it automatically and show where the models agree and where they do not.
cuerpo: On 16 November 2025, in ChatGPT-IA-edu, people were discussing the article “[Lo dice la IA, por lo tanto, puede no ser verdad](https://www.linkedin.com/posts/jvmanjon_iaparaeducaciaejn-ia-educaciaejn-activity-7395728593760280576-RKxK)” (in Spanish), by Juan Vicente García Manjón, on the risk of not checking what AI generates. One reply proposed “collegiate answers”: the same question to two or three AIs, another to detect discrepancies and a personal review of the process. It was also advised to ask the model to explain itself: that is almost always where you can see whether it is slipping.

Today that comes ready-made. On 5 February 2026, Perplexity introduced [Model Council](https://www.perplexity.ai/hub/blog/introducing-model-council): it sends the query to three models (in the announcement, Claude Opus 4.6, GPT 5.2 and Gemini 3.0) and another synthesises their answers, showing what they share and where they differ. It launched on the web and only for the Max subscription.

On 30 March 2026, Microsoft brought the idea to the Researcher agent in Microsoft 365 Copilot: in [Critique mode](https://support.microsoft.com/en-us/office/use-model-choice-in-the-researcher-agent), an OpenAI model drafts the report and an Anthropic one reviews it; in Model Council, both work at the same time and their agreements and differences are summarised. Both started out in the Frontier early-access programme. Cross-checking no longer means opening three tabs; reviewing is still up to the person.

piezas.comprobado: Mensaje #42154 de ChatGPT-IA-edu comprobado en t.me/ChatGPTedu/42154?embed=1 (16-11-2025): «respuestas colegiadas», 2 o 3 IA y otra para detectar discrepancias, revisión personal; #42151 (artículo de LinkedIn de Juan Vicente García Manjón) y #42160 (pedir explicaciones: «ahí casi siempre se ve si está patinando») en la entrada. Blog de Perplexity, abierto: Model Council, 5-2-2026, tres modelos por consulta (ejemplos Claude Opus 4.6, GPT 5.2, Gemini 3.0), un sintetizador indica coincidencias y diferencias; solo Max y web al lanzarse, móvil «próximamente». Entrada oficial del blog de Microsoft Tech Community, abierta: 30-3-2026, Critique (un modelo redacta, otro revisa; de OpenAI y Anthropic) y Council (ambos en paralelo y un juez resume acuerdos y diferencias), en el programa Frontier. Página de ayuda de Microsoft, abierta: describe los dos modos, sin fecha. Buscador del diario: nada publicado sobre Model Council ni Critique; tema y productos no repiten lo ya contado en «Hace un año». Medida: unas 240 palabras con la entradilla (recuento a mano).
